articles.title: White Sox Announce Munetaka Murakami Move Before Twins Finale
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox are getting ready for their finale with the Minnesota Twins, looking to bounce back after a tough loss on Saturday.So far, the two team...
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox are getting ready for their finale with the Minnesota Twins, looking to bounce back after a tough loss on Saturday.

So far, the two teams have split the first two games, with Chicago winning on Friday and the Twins taking the game last night. Entering the rubber match, the White Sox will be looking to grab the series win from their American League Central rivals.

Munetaka Murakami Decision Announced vs Twins

Ahead of the game, the White Sox have revealed the lineup to face the Twins. Within this, slugger Munetaka Murakami will be hitting third, playing first base.

Murakami has been a massive spark for the White Sox this season, and he will try to help his team grab another win in this contest.

Murakami was able to hit his 30th home run of the season in the team's loss on Saturday. But he didn't want to focus on that, instead desiring the win that the White Sox weren't able to record.

"Obviously I'm really happy about getting 30, but moreover we lost the game. So that's very much disappointing. We hope we can win one tomorrow," said Murakami . "If I can press down on the angle a little bit more, I think I can get better results. I hope we can continue that, and we can have better success tomorrow."

For the year, Murakami has hit .211 with 30 home runs and 61 RBIs, while posting an OPS of .832. His performance has been special, and it's been a big reason why Chicago is currently in a playoff spot.

In addition to Murakami , the White Sox had a few others hit their 30th home runs of the season recently. All-Star Miguel Vargas and Colson Montgomery did so on Friday, adding to the overall power on this roster.

White Sox manager Will Venable reflected on this feat from his players, showing praise for how they've played this season.

"It's really cool, it's special. Obviously, all these guys have done a great job really throughout our lineup," Venable said. "To have three guys in the middle of your lineup that have 30 homers, it means a lot. Obviously, it speaks to what we do well. These guys hit the ball hard, hit the ball over the fence, and it's cool to have three guys with 30."

Chicago will try to keep things rolling against the Twins, and this game could have a big impact on how the year unfolds. Every game matters at this time of the season, and the White Sox are fighting to make the playoffs.

Entering the game against the Twins, Chicago holds a record of 74-68 this season. They currently lead the AL Central by 2.5 games, with the Cleveland Guardians right behind them.

It will take a total team effort by the White Sox down the stretch to get into the playoffs. But this group has the utmost confidence in themselves, and they are currently in a great spot to compete the epic turnaround from last year.

articles.title: WSL investigating after Palace break substitution rules
articles.summary: The Women's Super League says an investigation is underway after Crystal Palace use four substitution windows in their win over Everton.
articles.body:
The Women's Super League says an investigation is under way after Crystal Palace used four substitution windows in their win over Everton.

A statement says that Palace "breached" the rules, adding that they only permit a maximum of three substitution opportunities per match.

The Eagles made four separate substitutions in the 62nd, 83rd, 90th and 97th minute of Sunday's 1-0 victory at the Borough Sports Ground.

The league confirmed the investigation will involve both clubs and referee body Pro Ref.

WSL rules do not prescribe an automatic punishment but any breach could be referred to an independent tribunal, which has the power to impose sanctions ranging from a warning or fine to a points deduction or other sporting sanction.

Both clubs have been approached for comment.
authors: Giulia Bould - BBC Radio Merseyside reporter

articles.title: Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong hits 40th home run to boost NL MVP case
articles.summary: Pete Crow-Armstrong became the youngest player in Chicago Cubs franchise history to hit 40 home runs.
articles.body:
In just a few weeks, Pete Crow-Armstrong is expected to join Ernie Banks in a select group: Chicago Cubs players who have won National League Most Valuable Player honors.

Yet PCA has already one-upped Mr. Cub in one category.

Crow-Armstrong became the youngest player in franchise history to hit 40 home runs, reaching the honor on Sunday, Sept. 6 with a low line drive just inside the right field foul pole at loanDepot Park, a game-tying fifth-inning shot off Miami Marlins right-hander Tyler Phillips.

While the Cubs would go on to lose the game 10-3, there's little to stop the Summer of PCA.

He's now second in the major leagues with 40 homers, trailing only Philadelphia DH Kyle Schwarber's 42, and his 8.6 WAR leads all position players. At 24 years, 165 days old, Crow-Armstrong is 49 days younger than Banks was when the Hall of Famer hit his 40th home run in 1955, the first of his eight consecutive All-Star seasons.

Banks would win NL MVP honors in 1958 - hitting a career-best and major league-high 47 homers - and 1959. He's one of 11 Cubs players to win the award.

Crow-Armstrong, with his .946 OPS, 33 stolen bases and defensive metrics that lap his rival center fielders, is expected to supplant the currently idled Shohei Ohtani , who won the past two NL MVPs.

For now, though, Crow-Armstrong has banked 40 homers for a club firmly entrenched in an NL playoff position.

"Forty homers, it's a hard number to get to," Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters in Miami. "And the season's not over."

articles.title: Geraldo Perdomo hit in head by line drive, exits with head contusion
articles.summary: Arizona Diamondbacks shortstop Geraldo Perdomo collapses after taking a 93 mph line drive directly to the helmet. Is he okay? Latest details
articles.body:
Arizona Diamondbacks shortstop Geraldo Perdomo left a Sunday, Sept. 6 game against the Houston Astros when he was hit by a teammate's line drive while on the basepaths.

Perdomo singled in the top of the third inning, and the next batter, Ketel Marte, hit an 93 mph line drive. Perdomo tried to get out of the way and covered up but was hit on the helmet. He dropped to the ground and was looked at by a trainer, eventually was helped up and left on his own power.

He was ruled out because he was hit by a batted ball. Nolan Arenado hit a two-run home run in the inning to give Arizona a 3-1 lead.

Perdomo was replaced at shortstop by Ildemaro Vargas, and Tim Tawa took Vargas' spot at first base.

The Diamondbacks announced Sunday that Perdomo suffered a head contusion on the play.

"He will continue to be monitored today and into tomorrow," the team said.

articles.title: Giants CB Greg Newsome makes his feelings clear about facing CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens
articles.summary: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II isn’t intimidated by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. His confident message — and past history with Pickens — just added eve...
articles.body:
The rivalry between the Dallas Cowboys and New York Giants may already have its first memorable quote of the 2026 NFL season.

Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II expressed plenty of respect for Dallas' dangerous wide receiver combination of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens ahead of their prime-time Week 1 matchup. However, Newsome made it clear he believes New York's secondary is capable of handling the challenge.

Newsome praised Pickens for his ability to make contested catches while pointing to Lamb's versatility as one of the qualities that makes him difficult to defend.

"Definitely great players, but I like our chances," Newsome said.

That final sentence could provide some additional motivation for a Cowboys offense expected to be among the NFL's most explosive units.

It also adds another chapter to Newsome's history with Pickens.

The two were involved in a confrontation during the 2024 season when Newsome played for the Cleveland Browns and Pickens was with the Pittsburgh Steelers . Their altercation occurred following Cleveland's Week 12 victory.

When Pickens was later asked about Newsome, the receiver dismissed the cornerback by saying he didn't know who he was. Newsome responded by questioning whether Pickens cared more about himself than his team.

Two years later, their paths have crossed again.

Pickens is now part of a Dallas receiving corps featuring Lamb, giving quarterback Dak Prescott two legitimate big-play weapons. Newsome, meanwhile, has joined a Giants defense looking to make major improvements after finishing 26th in points allowed last season.

New York enters a new era under head coach John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, and rebuilding the defense will be one of their biggest challenges.

Newsome certainly isn't lacking confidence.

His comments weren't necessarily disrespectful toward Dallas. In fact, he went out of his way to praise both receivers.

But rivalry games have a way of turning even the smallest comments into motivation.

When the Cowboys and Giants finally meet under the prime-time lights, Pickens may have another reason to remember exactly who Greg Newsome II is.

articles.title: As Week 1 Approaches, Browns Offensive Identity Still TBD
articles.summary: Todd Monken enters the regular season trusting his team's personnel, but still waiting to uncover the big picture of who the Cleveland Browns will be in 2026...
articles.body:
Every NFL coach hopes to know what their team does well this time of year.

When Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken wasn't navigating the QB1 battle between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders during training camp, he was trying to figure out exactly what the identity of his team is, particularly on offense.

The preseason is supposed to help uncover those things. But as Week 1 commences in the NFL, even Monken admitted he won't know the full picture of who his team is until they're in the thick of real games.

"I think we probably have more of an idea in terms of our personnel, per se, because we still go against each other. I think we're pretty good on defense, we went against the Bills," Monken explained. "But until we actually play, until we actually see it come together. I'm not sure we're there yet, but I like where we are at."

Essentially, Monken has a pretty good grasp of what personnel groupings his team operates best in. But their true strengths will reveal themselves once games start being played and the bullets are really flying.

It's not entirely uncommon for teams to need a few weeks of the regular season to really understand what its strengths and weaknesses are. Especially with the preseason often becoming a balancing act for coaches to keep their players healthy, while still trying to get them some valuable reps.

For Monken, his starters only saw minimal snaps in one preseason game, while also getting valuable work against the Bills during a joint practice. Otherwise, he chose to treat the third preseason game as an opportunity for the backups rather than a final dress rehearsal for his ones.

Monken downplayed the notion of a warm-up phase of the regular season.

"Our first two years in Baltimore, I'll just speak offensively, were a little sluggish, and then last year against the Bills, we were not," the former Ravens OC said. "Jacksonville didn't play their starters a heck of a lot more than we played ours, so it's equal. We're going to go into the same game, basically practicing against other teams, and I feel like we're going to be fine."

There are some context clues as to what the Browns will try to major in under Monken. For example, in each of the last three seasons Monken spent in Baltimore, his offense ranked top three in rushing. That's bound to be something he prioritizes here in Cleveland.

Ultimately, everyone will have a better sense of who the Browns are, Monken included, following Cleveland's Week 1 road showdown with the Jacksonville Jaguars. A r eturn trip to Florida to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers looms in Week 2.

articles.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua trending in right direction for Week 1
articles.summary: Rams WR Puka Nacua appears to be in line to play in the team's opener in Australia
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) is expected to play in the Week 1 game against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. Head coach Sean McVay said Sunday, Sept. 6, that the receiver is "making good progress."

"Been hitting some high speed yards at a really good clip with (head athletic trainer) Reggie [Scott] and his group," McVay said. "And when we get back out there, it'll be fun to have him."

Huddle Up: Fantasy managers can breathe a bit of a sigh of relief, but we're not out of the woods quite yet. We'll get a better sense of things Monday in the team's walkthrough, while things become a lot more definitive Tuesday into Wednesday, before an official injury designation is given. We have time, and with the Rams playing early in the week, there is time to formulate a plan. Have alternates at the ready just in case. If Nacua cannot go, Davante Adams would see a majority of the target share, with Jordan Whittington and perhaps the recently re-acquired Tutu Atwell stepping up.

articles.title: GB's Stevens wins Burghley for first time
articles.summary: Britain's Gemma Stevens claims the biggest win of her 25-year career with victory at Burghley Horse Trials.
articles.body:
Britain's Gemma Stevens won the Burghley Horse Trials for the first time on Sunday, the biggest victory of her career on her 31st attempt at five-star level.

The 41-year-old Olympian, riding Chilli Knight, cemented victory in executing a faultless showjumping round to finish on her dressage score of 29.6 - the only rider in the field to do so.

Compatriot Katie Magee finished second on Treworra, with USA's Caroline Pamukcu and HSH Blake in third.

"It's only taken me 25 years and finally I've managed to win a big B [Burghley or Badminton]. I couldn't be more proud," Stevens said.

Stevens, who first competed at the level in 2007, previously rode Chilli Knight's mother, King's Gem.

"It's unbelievable, I've known him [Chilli Knight] since the day he was born and this honestly means the absolute world," she said.

The win is redemption for Stevens after a disappointing World Championships in Aachen, Germany last month, when she failed to complete the cross-county event for the British team.

"Aachen was really tough, but that's sport. You've got to just bounce back and get on with it," she added.

Stevens and Chilli Knight previously won the replacement five-star event at Bicton in 2021, after Covid cancelled Burghley.

articles.title: Report: New York Giants agree to $22M extension with OL Jon Runyan
articles.summary: The New York Giants and OL Jon Runyan reportedly agreed to a $22 million contract extension.
articles.body:
The New York Giants continued their fall version of spring cleaning as it pertains to the salary cap, reportedly agreeing to a contract extension with veteran guard Jon Runyan.

Almost immediately after agreeing to an extension with backup quarterback Jameis Winston , the Giants elected to lock up one of their starters along the offensive line just before the start of the season.

The deal, first reported by ESPN's Adam Schefter, is a two-year extension worth $22 million. It also includes $21.5 million guaranteed for the 29-year-old.

Runyan has spent the last two seasons working as a starter for the Giants as the team's starting left guard. According to Pro Football Focus, Runyan allowed 31 total pressures, including two sacks, on 654 pass-blocking snaps during the 2025 season.

Runyan will reprise his role as the starter sandwiched between left tackle Andrew Thomas and the polarizing John Michael Schmitz at center.

The Giants offensive line will need to protect its young quarterback in Jaxson Dart, who enters his second season in the NFL. Though Runyan may not provide All-Pro level play, the continuity should help the Giants as they enter an interesting campaign under a new regime.

articles.title: Andy Borregales returning to football roots with jersey number change
articles.summary: Andy Borregales has recently made the switch to No. 8.
articles.body:
Worn by leading wide receiver Stefon Diggs, the No. 8. jersey was a big part of the New England Patriots' 2025 campaign. With less than a week before the 2026 season opener, however, it remained vacant.

For Andy Borregales, that was all the opportunity he needed. The second-year kicker, who had started his NFL career wearing No. 36, recently adopted the number in what is a return to his personal football roots.

"It was the first number I ever wore when I started playing football at five years old," Borregales told reporters in the Patriots locker room on Sunday. "I kind of waited until the end; if anyone was going to get it, go get it. I saw that it was still available, so I was like, 'I might as well just try to get it,' and here we are."

Borregales recalled wearing the No. 8 jersey all the way up until middle school. When his older brother José left for high school, however, he decided to pick up his old No. 30 jersey. From that point on, he found himself kicking in the 30s rather than the single digits.

That remained the case throughout his stint at the University of Miami, where he again followed in his brother's footsteps, and into the NFL. Wearing No. 36, Borregales made 31 of 38 field goal tries as well as 60 of 62 extra points as a sixth-round rookie.

Like his predecessor in the No. 8, he therefore had an active hand in the Patriots' fortunes last season. But unlike Stefon Diggs, Borregales is still around: whereas the veteran wideout was cut in March and has since joined the Washington Commanders, the 23-year-old place kicker is locked into his position on New England's current roster trying to be a worthy wearer of his new digit.

"I had a great relationship with him," Borregales said of Diggs. "I hope he's doing good in Washington, and I do believe he's going to be doing good. He was a great guy. He was a good locker room guy."

Borregales is entering his second season in Foxborough off a generally solid summer, albeit one that saw him miss three kicks in the preseason opener against the Colts. He was perfect in the two exhibition games since, but that single performance nonetheless raised questions about his readiness.

For his coordinator, Jeremy Springer, there is nothing to be concerned about.

"Oh, he's ready to go. I don't have any doubts in Andy not being ready to go," Springer said. "He's a very mature athlete as a kicker and he prepares that way. He never gets too high or too low. I've seen that a million times here, whether it's a good game, bad game, good practice, bad practice, he learns from it, he studies it and he comes back better the next day."

Borregales will be asked to do so again this season. The only difference is that it will be in a new number that very much is an old one for him.

articles.title: Pass Rushers’ Absence is Telling Sign About Georgia’s Defense
articles.summary: Georgia's pass rush struggled against Tennessee State as star rookie Chase Linton sat out with an injury. Here is why the Bulldogs need him back now.
articles.body:
Chase Linton did not play in Saturday's game because of a lower leg injury, leaving Georgia with a thin pass rush that managed only three sacks. Coach Kirby Smart confirmed the injury and stated the team hopes to get him back soon. This absence is a major problem for a defense that needs to improve its pressure on the quarterback.

A Promising Rookie Sits on the Sidelines

The loss of Linton hurts more than just the lineup for one game. DawgNation reported that Linton had a strong offseason and consistently earned praise from the coaching staff before the injury struck. This year, the improved Georgia pass rush was expected to feature him significantly. Without him, the unit lacks the depth and talent needed to dominate.

Smart told reporters that the Bulldogs "hope to get him back." That is a relief, but hope does not stop opposing quarterbacks. The team needs him on the field now, not later. Georgia only had 20.0 sacks last season, so adding a player of his caliber is vital. The coaching staff knows they cannot afford to wait too long for his return.

Three Sacks Is Not Enough for a Top Team

Georgia finished with just 3.0 sacks against Tennessee State. That number is too low for a team with championship aspirations. The Bulldogs dominated the game with a 63-3 victory, but the defense did not pressure the quarterback enough. AJC.com covered the injury report, listing Linton alongside other players like Jontae Gilbert who also missed time.

The injury list shows a pattern of minor issues, but Linton's absence is the most concerning. His role was to help fix the sack total that plagued the team last year. If he cannot play, the defense must find a way to generate pressure without him. The numbers from last season prove that 20.0 sacks is not an acceptable standard for this program.

Georgia must adjust its scheme to get more sacks without Linton. The coaching staff cannot rely on the same plan that produced only three sacks. DawgNation noted that the team needs to find a solution quickly.

articles.title: Newly acquired Lakers forward reveals shocking team chemistry
articles.summary: A newly acquired Lakers forward reveals the shocking chemistry of the team.Sandro Mamukelashvili has yet to wear his Lakers uniform in an NBA game but is alr...
articles.body:
Sandro Mamukelashvili has yet to wear his Lakers uniform in an NBA game but is already making the most of his time with the team.

Mamukelashvili appeared in an interview on the golf course with Deondre Hawkins of ESPN and spoke about the team's recent trip to Luka Dončić's home country of Slovenia .

"First of all, shoutout to Luka. I think the organization was amazing, the way they planned everything," Mamukelashvili said. "They showed us a lot of great places, and Ljubljana is a really, really nice city."

"Plus, it was great for the new team. It was a bunch of new guys on the team, and you know, all of us being together, it didn't even feel like it was a lot of new guys."

Mamukelashvili said the team jelled well, and he left feeling excited for this season because of how excited everyone else was.

Aside from the trip, Mamukelashvili and his Lakers teammates have been spotted golfing throughout the offseason. He was asked who is the team's second-best golfer after Austin Reaves.

"I've been hearing a lot about Bronny [James]," Mamukelashvili said. "They say he's really, really good, and that he actually plays a lot. … So I'm kind of looking forward to seeing the Luka, Austin, Bronny tournament."

The new Lakers forward was one of the key depth pieces Rob Pelinka , the team's president of basketball operations, made over the offseason. Mamukelashvili will join the team as a sixth-year veteran after bouncing around the league with the Bucks, Spurs and Raptors.

Mamukelashvili is a year removed from a career high, averaging 11.2 points per game, as well as 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists.

While the Lakers are enjoying their time off the basketball court, the NBA season is rapidly approaching. The team is expected to report for training camp on Sept. 29.

The 2026-2027 season is a pivotal year for the Lakers, who are transitioning to new ownership for the second season in a row .

They are also about to enter a new era of Lakers basketball that features the team fully embracing Dončić as the main guy after LeBron James' departure during the offseason .

articles.title: Czech Open darts results: Luke Littler beats Luke Humphries to win
articles.summary: Luke Littler overcomes defending champion Luke Humphries to claim the Czech Open title on the European Tour.
articles.body:
Luke Littler overcame defending champion Luke Humphries to claim the Czech Open title in Prague.

World number one Littler was playing in his first European Tour event since the Belgium Open in March, and beat Krzysztof Ratajski, Danny Noppert as well as Michael van Gerwen on his way to the blockbuster final.

He was trailing 4-3 against world number two Humphries, who saw off Andrew Gilding, William O'Connor and Gerwyn Price, before a four-leg burst put the 19-year-old Littler 7-4 in front.

Humphries reduced the deficit to 7-6 but failed to level the match as he missed with two darts at double 16 in the 14th leg.

Littler capitalised by taking out 39 for a win which secures his place at the European Championship in Dortmund in October.

"This is what the fans are in for - me and Luke are back," said Littler.

"The two best going at it in a final once again. I'm glad I've won.

"It's good to be back and I'm back with a bang.

"These long days are worth it, especially lifting the trophy."

Littler, who is attempting to complete the calendar sweep of ranking events in 2026, added: "I think I've secured my place in Dortmund - Dortmund is the one I'm chasing."

Humphries was aiming to win the Czech Open for a fourth time and third occasion on the trot.

"I was going to pull out Thursday, and I made the final, so I can't be too upset with myself because I did really well," he said.

"I never give up, especially in finals. I know that Luke is obviously going to throw everything at me.

"Hopefully over the next four months, I push him. If he does the clean sweep, he has to do it the hard way."

images.caption: Image caption, Luke Littler, right, earned £35,000 for winning the Czech Open

articles.title: Caitlin Clark goes without scoring a field goal for first time in her career as Team USA wins narrowly against Italy
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark once again came off the bench for Team USA in their group stage game against Italy at the FIBA World Cup. However, this time around, she wasn’t...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark once again came off the bench for Team USA in their group stage game against Italy at the FIBA World Cup. However, this time around, she wasn't able to show off her brilliance as she did in the game against China, where she scored 14 points and had 11 assists.

In a game against the 14th-placed FIBA nation, USA came out with a narrow 55-52 win, but Clark looked miles off her best as she only scored 1 point.

Jackie Young and Angel Reese, who came off the bench, were pivotal for Team USA. They scored 10 and 8 points respectively, with Reese also recording two blocks and a steal against Italy.

Clark was expected to have another big night, but she just never got going as the Italian defense made it hard for her to score.

Clark fails to score a field goal for the first time in her career

The Indiana Fever player is known for her ability to score. She is averaging 22.5 PPG with the team in the WNBA, and after her performance against China, it seemed like the same version of her would be available throughout the tournament.

However, Clark could only score off a free throw against Italy, as she missed all six of her field goal attempts.

This was the first time in her career that Clark went without scoring a field goal, according to ESPN Insights.

She has always scored with ease, which is why her records in college were sensational.

Clark carried that same form into the WNBA and is now one of the best players in the league.

It was visible that the team struggled without her firepower, as they made it tough for themselves against the Italians

Clark will be hoping that she returns in top form for Team USA's next game against the Czech Republic.

articles.title: Giants, QB Jameis Winston agree to two-year extension
articles.summary: No. 1 overall pick in 2015 embraces his status as No. 2 on the depth chart.
articles.body:
The No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 draft continues to embrace his status as a No. 2 quarterback.

Per multiple reports, the Giants and Jameis Winston have agreed to terms on a two-year, $13 million extension.

The move puts Winston under contract through 2028, as the clear backup to Jaxson Dart.

Winston became the Week 1 starter as a rookie in Tampa. After five seasons with the Buccaneers, he spent four years with the Saints (starting 10 games), one with the Browns (starting seven), and one with the Giants (starting two).

In lieu of finishing his current deal and becoming a free agent in March 2027 (where he could have potentially found a spot to compete for a starting role), Winston decided to stay put, with a total commitment of three years.

It doesn't hurt Winston to be in New York, given that he seems to be destined to become a star in the media space, once his playing career ends.

articles.title: Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover details bloody nose incident against North Texas
articles.summary: Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover discussed his bloody nose scare after Saturday's game.
articles.body:
Indiana had its way with North Texas on Saturday, but not before quarterback Josh Hoover had a bloody nose scare.

During the second quarter of the game, North Texas brought pressure, resulting in a defender grabbing Hoover's facemask and turning his helmet fully backward. Hoover immediately started bleeding, and the blood kept dripping from his nose.

The defender was penalized 15 yards for a facemask penalty.

Hoover stayed in the game and threw a touchdown pass to Charlie Becker to cap off the drive. Becker's touchdown extended Indiana's lead to 21-3 before the program went on to win 52-16.

After the game, Hoover went into detail about the facemask, saying it looked "way worse than it felt."

"It looked way worse than it felt," Hoover said . "I didn't even know it was bleeding like that, but no, I feel good."

He also confirmed that he felt the blood and that he was alright.

Hoover finished the game with 231 yards through the air and four touchdowns. It was his first start with the Hoosiers after previously playing for TCU.

Indiana will continue its non-conference schedule next Saturday against Howard, then play its third and final non-conference game on Sept. 19 against Western Kentucky.

Kickoff for next Saturday's game against Howard will be at noon ET on the Big Ten Network.

articles.title: Team USA avoids upset, clinches quarterfinal berth at FIBA World Cup
articles.summary: The U.S. women's team narrowly avoided its first World Cup loss since the 2006 semifinals.
articles.body:
Jackie Young had a big fourth quarter and Breanna Stewart made her only basket of the game to put the United States up for good, helping the Americans escape with a 55-52 win over Italy in the FIBA Women's World Cup on Sunday, Sept. 6 in Berlin.

The U.S. (2-0), which clinched a quarterfinal berth with the victory, led only 42-39 after three quarters and fell behind by two three times in the fourth. Stewart's jumper, assisted by Young, gave the Americans a 51-50 lead with 3:20 to go, and Young hit a floater on their next possession.

Chelsea Gray made a shot with 1:07 left for some important cushion, but Italy hit a quick 2-pointer in response to cut it to 55-52. Gray missed a shot on the next U.S. trip but Young corralled the rebound to help her team bleed more clock.

Italy's Cecilia Zandalasini, who missed a 3-pointer to tie with three seconds left, was seen hollering at referees after the buzzer as she argued she had been poked in the eye on the play.

Young scored six of her team-high 10 points in the fourth quarter. Angel Reese scored eight points, Stewart grabbed 11 rebounds to help offset her 1-for-9 shooting day, and Paige Bueckers added seven points, five boards, two assists, two steals and two blocks for the U.S.

Caitlin Clark shot 0-for-6 from the floor and scored one point.

The Americans won despite shooting a woeful 16 of 56 (28.6%) overall and 1-for-12 on 3-pointers. They outscored the Italians 22-14 at the foul line.

Zandalasini of the WNBA's Golden State Valkyries had 14 points and seven boards to guide Italy (1-1).

The U.S. women's team narrowly avoided its first World Cup loss since the 2006 semifinals. It marked their closest World Cup game in 20 years, per NBC Sports.

The U.S. concludes Group D play Monday, Sept. 7 against the Czech Republic (0-2). The other game will pit Italy against China (1-1). While group winners (including the U.S.) advance directly to the quarterfinals of the knockout stage, the second- and third-place finishers of each group will go on to a qualification round.

articles.title: Steelers could face Falcons fourth-string QB in Week 1
articles.summary: Steelers could face 4th-string QB in Week 1
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers open their season in t-minus one week against the Atlanta Falcons. Pittsburgh has never lost to Atlanta at home, and it will mark the third time in the last 16 years the two teams have faced one another in Week 1.

It's not controversial at all to say the Steelers are the more talented team, but they may have an even bigger advantage when the ball is kicked off next Sunday.

There is a real possibility that the Steelers will face Atlanta's fourth-string quarterback, as John Fricke of 92.9 The Game in Atlanta points out.

"One week out [and the] Falcons have not yet named a starter," Fricke posted on X . "Tua did not win the job. Rush is a back-up. If Penix is a physical 'no go,' do they have time to prep Jack Strand [with] the first-team to go vs. the Steelers?"

Strand is a rookie from Division-II Minnesota Moorhead. He was a D-II All-American in 2025. He finished his collegiate career with an astounding 13,161 yards and 126 touchdowns.

While he was an undrafted rookie, the Falcons may feel more comfortable with Strand after seeing what Tua Tagovailoa showed them in preseason play – a stretch of play that reportedly made him "impossible" to start in the eyes of the Falcons, via Ian Rapoport .

articles.title: Kamden Sixkiller throws for 330 yards and 2 touchdowns as Campbell beats Western Carolina 28-19
articles.summary: Kamden Sixkiller threw for 330 yards and two touchdowns, Spencer Jones had a career-high 126 yards receiving and a score, and Campbell beat Western Carolina...
articles.body:
BUIES CREEK, N.C. (AP) — Kamden Sixkiller threw for 330 yards and two touchdowns, Spencer Jones had a career-high 126 yards receiving and a score, and Campbell beat Western Carolina 28-19 on Sunday in a game postponed due to weather.

Campbell is off to its first 2-0 start since 2018 after securing the program's second victory over an FCS top 25 opponent. WCU entered ranked No. 24 in the Stats Perform FCS Top 25 poll after beating Eastern Kentucky on Aug. 29.

Campbell scored a touchdown on its first two drives before taking a 21-3 lead early in the second quarter on a 1-yard run by Ethan Lawrence that was set up by a 43-yard strike from Sixkiller to Brady Ambrose. Sixkiller also found Ambrose for a 6-yard TD to cap a 10-play, 91-yard drive to start the game, and Sixkiller scored on an 8-yard run for a 14-0 lead.

Sixkiller finished 29-of-44 passing with three interceptions for Campbell. JJ Cowan had a team-high 83 yards on the ground. The Camels posted 528 yards of total offense for their second straight game with 500-plus.

Lex Thomas was 25-of-44 passing for 326 yards and two touchdowns for Western Carolina (1-1). Both of Jai Boyd's catches were for touchdowns.

WCU was held to 1-yard rushing — the second fewest allowed in Campbell's program history. The Catamounts were also 2 of 13 on third down.

The game was originally scheduled for Saturday, when it was delayed over two hours due to lightning in the area. Then an electrical issue caused one of the stadium's four main light banks to malfunction and force the postponement.

Western Carolina: At Cincinnati on Saturday.

articles.title: 71-73 – Rangers put on their rally pants to take finale from Rays 8-6
articles.summary: Six innings of one-run relief keys Texas to victory
articles.body:
The Texas Rangers scored eight runs while the Tampa Bay Rays scored six runs.

We had ourselves a certified Gore Inning (TM) today and it was a particularly bloody one as Rangers starter MacKenzie Gore was disemboweled for four runs in the top of the second inning.

The Rays loaded up on singles and let the Rangers make some questionable defensive decisions to collect their early lead. Up big early, it seemed like the Rangers were destined to another loss against Tampa Bay which would have sealed a series defeat to the AL's top club. However, Jake Burger had other ideas.

The Rangers first baseman hit a solo home run to get the Rangers on the board and following another Rays run in the top of the third, Burger smacked his second homer, a two-run shot this time, to pull Texas to within a couple of runs.

MacKenzie was run out of the game after just three innings, which put a lot of pressure on the bullpen to work through some innings. They were mostly up to the task with latest arm Trevor Williams tossing two scoreless, Chase Silseth pitching in for a scoreless inning, and Tyler Alexander working out of a jam having allowed a run.

By the time Alexander allowed Tampa Bay's sixth run, the Rangers had fully rallied and overtaken the Rays. In the same inning following Burger's second dong, the Rangers got a few on base and Justin Foscue fought off a two-strike pitch to sneak a ball on the fair side of the line for a two-out, two-run double that tied the game.

The next inning Burger started a rally with a walk and after a Logan O'Hoppe single, the Rangers took the lead for good via an Elias Diaz single that scored Burger. The Rangers weren't done there, though, as following the inning's second out, Ezequiel Duran singled to drive in a run and give Texas a bit of a cushion.

After Alexander allowed Tampa Bay's sixth run in the top of the seventh, the Rangers turned to Jacob Latz in the eighth inning with the top of the Rays' lineup due in a one run game. The Rangers had been burned in some games recently waiting for their chance to use Latz in a traditional closer situation. Today they switched things up and used Latz in a set up role when things looked most dangerous.

After pitching two innings yesterday, Latz worked around a single and got through the eighth scoreless on 18 pitches. The Rangers opted to go with Jakob Junis for the save after Corey Seager reinvested in some insurance with a solo home run in the bottom of the eighth. With a two run lead in the ninth, Junis nailed down the victory and the Rangers finished off the series with a split despite the big early deficit today.

All in all, a series win would have been preferable but the Rangers were competitive against the league leaders all weekend and remain in the hunt for one of the playoff spots in the American League with three weeks left in the season.

Player of the Game : Burger was responsible for Texas' first three runs via a couple of home runs which helped the Rangers claw their way out of an early hole. Burger also scored the go-ahead run in the bottom of the fifth.

Up Next : The Rangers have Mondays off every week this month, including tomorrow. They will venture up to Seattle to take on the scuffling Mariners beginning on Tuesday night.

articles.title: Seahawks-Patriots preview: Pats insider details key offseason changes
articles.summary: Get a Patriots reporter’s viewpoint of what has changed for the AFC champions since losing to the Seahawks in Super Bowl 60.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks' 2026 regular season begins with a familiar opponent, but I don't think Seattle can approach Wednesday night as if it is simply picking up where Super Bowl 60 ended. For the first regular-season edition of "Eye on the Prey" as part of The Hawks Eye podcast , I was joined by Taylor Kyles of Patriots Daily to take a deeper look at what has changed in New England and what Seattle should expect when the Patriots arrive at Lumen Field for Week 1.

Roster changes, plus another year for Drake Maye

The biggest difference is the amount of talent New England has added around Drake Maye. The Patriots made an aggressive move for A.J. Brown, added Romeo Doubs from the Green Bay Packers to the receiving corps and strengthened the offensive line with former New York Jets guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, allowing the Patriots to move Jared Wilson from left guard to center. Defensively, veterans such as safety Kevin Byard and former Seahawks pass rusher Dre'Mont Jones give Mike Vrabel additional flexibility. This was already a 14-win team last season, so the offseason was less about rebuilding and more about addressing the areas that kept New England from finishing the job against Seattle in February.

"I think one of the biggest things was the offensive line," Kyles said. "And look, that wasn't a secret going in. Will Campbell had a sprained MCL and was playing next to Jared Wilson, so you had two rookies on one side of the line of scrimmage. Garrett Bradbury had been pretty solid for what the expectations were, but you kind of knew that he wasn't exactly a strength for that unit. He was really just kind of holding the spot for a season. Morgan Moses, I mean, the guy's 36 years old. As you can imagine, I think when you look back at the tape, honestly, looking back recently, it really stood out. It was like, Morgan's a good player, but for a guy that age, all those games it really did add up. And I think it kind of showed in his plays. So, the offensive line clearly needed reinforcements. It needed its younger players to take a step forward."

Taylor and I spent a good portion of the conversation discussing how those additions could change the chess match between Maye and Mike Macdonald. Seattle's defense created problems last season through disguise, simulated pressure and post-snap rotation. A.J. Brown now gives Maye a receiver who can win even when the coverage is technically sound, which could force Seattle to make some difficult decisions about how aggressively it wants to pressure while also protecting against explosive plays.

"[The red zone offense] looks like it's going to be more potent. And obviously that starts with AJ Brown because all you need is the twofer in the red zone. If you're a threat on a slant and you're a threat on a fade, very hard to defend that. But you've also seen Romeo Doubs have a lot of success in the red zone, which isn't a surprise. He's been kind of a red zone merchant his entire career."

Another year in Josh McDaniel's offense could also provide valuable experience for the MVP runner-up.

"A major emphasis for the Patriots offense this offseason is incorporating tempo, having Drake get to the line of scrimmage and different types of tempo. It's not always 'let's go as fast as we can and just call a play.' Sometimes it's 'let's get to the line of scrimmage, dummy call, see what they're in, and then try to get ourselves in good position.' So, the biggest things for me really and obviously like receiver, we can kind of hit on that, but really it was the trenches and it was Drake Maye between the ears, just a lack of experience that really got exposed as he got into the game and you felt like, all right, they're not running the ball. Everyone knows what's going on. Is Drake going to take what they give him? Is he gonna kind of panic a little bit? And you saw the inexperience."

A cornerback matchup the Seahawks could exploit

On the other side, this will be our first opportunity to see Brian Fleury's offense in a meaningful regular-season game. New England still has plenty of high-end defensive talent, particularly in the secondary with Christian Gonzalez, and its interior defensive front has the ability to disrupt an offense without requiring constant pressure packages. How Fleury uses motion, play-action and formations to create favorable matchups will be one of the most fascinating parts of Week 1. Taylor did note one possible wide receiver vs. cornerback matchup that would worry him from a Patriots perspective.

"I didn't like Rashid Shaheed versus Carlton Davis before the Super Bowl," Kyles said. "I was pretty clear about that. I did not think that was a good matchup for the Patriots. Maybe it didn't manifest that way, but like you mentioned, he's even better, and Carlton Davis missed most of training camp. In some of the joint practices, quite frankly, he was getting kind of cooked off the line in a way that slightly concerned me. Mow Marcus Jones, if they match up, I like it. I think if Rashid Shaheed's going to go up and make an impressive catch, awesome. But I think Marcus would be on his hip. He's one of the most explosive players at that position. If Marcus Jones were three inches taller, he'd be a Pro Bowler. Like, he's a phenomenal player. It's just he's small and there's only so much you can do at that size, and even then he still makes plays.

"I don't like it because unless Carlton Davis gets his hands on Rashid Shaheed, he just can't run with him. That's the reality. He's an older corner. Again, he's a pro and I think technically there's a lot of things he can do to kind of even that matchup a little bit. But if Sam Darnold decides that he wants to really test that matchup, I have a hard time thinking that he's not going to get some results he likes."

We also went through New England's offseason, training camp and preseason, the Patriots' remaining roster questions, the matchups that could ultimately decide the game, and our keys to victory.

This may be a Super Bowl rematch, but both teams have evolved since February. That is what makes Wednesday night so interesting!

articles.title: Carmelo Anthony was 'willing' to take pay cut to stay in OKC for 2nd year
articles.summary: Carmelo Anthony was 'willing' to take pay cut to stay in OKC for 2nd year.
articles.body:
After an unceremonious Round 1 exit, the Oklahoma City Thunder were ready for change. One of the more polarizing iterations of the small-market franchise happened in the 2017-18 season. Akin to a superhero movie, they provided Russell Westbrook with help from a couple of star-studded names in Paul George and Carmelo Anthony.

Recovering from Kevin Durant's shocking 2016 departure, Westbrook provided a much-needed distraction and a highly entertaining brand of hoops. As the undisputed best player, he averaged a historic 30-point triple-double en route to his sole MVP award.

Alas, Westbrook's one-man show wasn't enough to build a contender. The Thunder knew this the moment Durant jumped ship, but they needed to get some serious star power. In comes George — who requested a trade from the Indiana Pacers. And eventually, Anthony — who did the same with the New York Knicks.

Westbrook, George and Anthony were a blockbuster trio in name, but on the court, they never meshed well. The Thunder went on to have an inconsistent 48-34 record and lost to the Utah Jazz in another Round 1 loss. After paying for the most expensive roster in NBA history at the time, OKC had to move on from Anthony. Especially since it needed to sign George to a contract extension.

According to Anthony, the Thunder were hell-bent on moving on from him. Even if he tried to finagle the NBA's cap-space rules to stick around. He detailed his divorce from OKC on Dwyane Wade's Feb. 2024 podcast episode .

"That summer, I was supposed to sign back. I still had a year left from OKC. I was going back to OKC," Anthony said. "I start hearing the whispers, 'Hey, you want to restructure your contract?' I'm owed $28 million. I said, 'Y'all want me to restructure this? How do y'all want me to restructure? I want to be here. I'm willing to do what I've got to do to be here. I want to build me, PG and Russ.'"

On Anthony's original contract when he first joined the Thunder, he had an expiring $27.9 million salary for the 2018-19 season. That obviously was not attainable to have on your books. Especially if he was going to be a bench player. That type of salary is for a borderline All-Star player. Not somebody on the downward slope of their career.

"I'm willing to do that. I'll take less. What kind of deal do y'all want? You want to cut this down into three years? 28 over three? Let's do four years. Give me seven a year," Anthony said. "Let's do it. I'm gonna work with it."

It's easy to see why the Thunder gave Anthony the cold shoulder. Even after he tried to work his way around his bloated salary. There were just no salvageable paths to go to. So OKC traded him to the Atlanta Hawks in a three-team deal. Eventually, his contract was bought out.

"They were trying to figure out a way to make the contracts work for everybody. At this point, I was owed 28 at one year, my last year. PG had deals coming," Anthony said. "So I'm talking to them like, 'Yo, P, y'all want to be here, Russ? We gonna make this work. I'm gonna break my deal down.'"

Afterward, Anthony signed with the Houston Rockets on a one-year deal. They were the team most linked to him in his 2017 summer sweepstakes. Of course, most know about Anthony's notoriously short stint there. He didn't even make it to Thanksgiving before they pulled the plug on that experiment. He was sent home and eventually played three more years in a bench role with the Portland Trail Blazers and Los Angeles Lakers before retiring.

Things just didn't work out between Anthony and the Thunder. He struggled to excel in a third-option role. He averaged 16.2 points on 40.4% shooting and 5.8 rebounds. And in the 2018 NBA playoffs, he was borderline unplayable. At that point, the best course of action is to just move on. It was the right call by OKC.

articles.title: How Charlie Woods fared in final round of Junior Players Championship
articles.summary: Charlie Woods tied for eighth at the Junior Players Championship, marking his best national finish since 2025.
articles.body:
Charlie Woods enjoyed his best finish of the 2026 season this weekend at the Junior Players Championship.

Woods, a senior at the Benjamin School and son of legendary golfer Tiger Woods , shot 71 (1-under) in the final round on Sunday, Sept. 6 at TPC Sawgrass in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida.

He finished at 1-under overall and tied for eighth across the three-round event. JP Lynch of Austin, Texas won the event at 8-under.

Woods finished his tournament with the type of round that has been characteristic of his tournament appearance, offsetting five birdies with four bogeys. Overall, he carded 14 birdies and 13 bogeys in the event.

Here are some highlights from his final round:

On No. 10, Woods nearly holed out his approach shot for an eagle and carded birdie.

On No. 11, he sunk a 15-foot birdie putt to pull into the tournament top 10.

After a par on No. 12, he ran into tough luck, lipping out on birdie putts at No. 13, 14 and 15.

On No. 16, he hooked his tee shot deep into the trees and punched out to later save par.

On the famous "Island Green," Woods played long and left, two-putting from 25 feet.

The Junior Players Championship will go down as undeniable success for Woods. It's his best finish in a junior golf tournament with a national field since he won the 2025 Team TaylorMade Invitational at Streamsong Resort (Black) in Bowling Green, Florida.

Woods also made news on Friday by signing with one of the world's biggest golf brands. He formally announced an NIL contract with TaylorMade via social media with multiple promotional videos.

Final: Out 37, In 34, Total 71 (1-under)

articles.title: 3 aha moments from BYU’s Week 1 victory over Utah Tech
articles.summary: Here are three plays that set BYU on a course to quickly turn opening night into a glorified pre-game workout for next week’s Big 12 opener against Arizona.
articles.body:
There was little doubt prior to kickoff that BYU's season opener against Utah Tech wasn't going to go exactly as it went. The No. 14-ranked Cougars, a seven-touchdown favorite, overwhelmed the Trailblazers in all phases of the game to win by eight touchdowns, 63-7.

Along the way, there were three key plays that set BYU on a course to quickly turn opening night into a glorified pre-game workout for next week's Big 12 opener against Arizona . Here they are:

Cannon DeVries had dreamed about just such a moment growing up in North Ogden and playing football at Weber High — he wanted to get to LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo and return a kickoff for a touchdown.

Saturday night against Utah Tech — his moment came.

Determined for a return, DeVries fielded the second-half kickoff a couple of steps inside his own end zone. Once he reached the 7-yard line, he veered away from the right side to the left. On the way, he shook off a would-be tackler around the 15.

"After the first guy missed, I made a couple of more guys miss and saw the comeback open, so I made a move," said DeVries. By the time he reached the Y logo at midfield, "it was green grass from there. I knew I was gone."

"You don't feel your legs the last 20 yards," he said. "It's like a 400-meter dash. You are just running with whatever is left in the tank."

The 6-foot-0, 184-pound sophomore, who also started at cornerback, had more than enough fuel to get him there to give BYU a 49-0 lead.

True freshman Legend Glasker made quite a first impression at BYU, scoring three touchdowns in his debut, including two on his first two touches — a 9-yard run and a 26-yard reception in the first quarter. However, it was his third touchdown, a 33-yard grab in the second quarter, that put him in a rare place.

"The people around me, the coaches and players, they bought into me a lot, and they trust me," said the former Lehi High star. "So, I feel like when they entrusted me, I can just really go out there and do this with their trust. I feel like I can do anything."

Glasker became the first BYU freshman to score three or more touchdowns in a game since 2012 when Jamaal Williams (who watched from the sideline) scored four times against Georgia Tech. Glasker is also the first BYU player with three touchdowns in a half since Keanu Hill pulled it off — also against Utah Tech in 2022.

A legendary start for a young player with big plans and with a wise quarterback who isn't much older than he is.

"Bear Bachmeier is just so smart," Glasker said. "I feel like his smarts help me do better on the field — just looking at the defense and seeing what he wants me to do."

Glasker isn't the only one using three fingers to count up his big plays. Senior cornerback Evan Johnson intercepted Utah Tech's CJ Tiller early in the second quarter for his third interception in his last four games.

Johnson turned momentum in BYU's favor against UCF last November with an interception in the second quarter. He saved the game at the Pop-Tarts Bowl against Georgia Tech with an interception in the end zone with 14 seconds remaining.

On Saturday, Johnson's diving grab was part of a four-takeaway night for the defense — the most for BYU in a season opener since 2003 — back when the dynamic defender was only 2 years old.

Dave McCann is a sportswriter and columnist for the Deseret News and is a play-by-play announcer and show host for BYUtv/ESPN+. He co-hosts "Y's Guys" at ysguys.com and is the author of the children's book "C is for Cougar," available at deseretbook.com.

articles.title: Jak Jones shocks Mark Selby to win British Open title
articles.summary: Jak Jones claims the second ranking title of his career by beating four-time world champion Mark Selby 10-6 in the British Open final.
articles.body:
Jak Jones claimed the second ranking title of his career by beating four-time world champion Mark Selby 10-6 in the British Open final.

The pair were tied at 4-4 after the afternoon session, which included a 139 from Selby.

Another century break brought Selby level at 5-5 before Jones, who beat Judd Trump in the semi-final, started to pull away by moving into a two frame lead at 7-5.

Breaks of 53 and 62 put Jones one frame from victory and, after England's Selby missed a green on the colours, the Welshman secured victory.

"I can't believe it to be honest," Jones, who won his first ranking title with victory at the 2026 Championship League in July, told Channel 5.

"I never thought I'd be able to grind Mark Selby down but I've done it today."

Jones turned professional at 16 in 2010 and briefly dropped off the World Snooker Tour twice before becoming a mainstay since 2016.

He reached the 2024 World Championship final but was beaten by Kyren Wilson.

"It's been difficult for the last 15 years - I've been battling away. For my parents, wife and son, it's unbelievable because I haven't really achieved a lot in the game.

"This season, to start winning things just feels amazing."

articles.title: Italy’s upset bid falls short as the US escapes 55-52 in a tense World Cup game
articles.summary: Italy came close to pulling off one of the biggest upsets in women's FIBA World Cup history.  The Italians, making their first appearance in the tournament s...
articles.body:
BERLIN (AP) — Italy came close to pulling off one of the biggest upsets in women's FIBA World Cup history.

The Italians, making their first appearance in the tournament since 1994, gave the U.S. all it could handle before falling 55-52 on Sunday. It was the fewest points the Americans had scored in a World Cup win since they beat Australia 42-38 in 1967.

Italy (1-1) almost handed the Americans their first loss in the tournament since 2006 and first preliminary round defeat since 1983. Instead they came up just a few plays short.

"I feel a little bitter of course but they were the better team and they made better plays at the end so they deserve to win," Italy point guard Mariella Santucci said. "I feel like the way we play we learn so much about ourselves that we can compete against everybody. To play like that with the USA is special, but it makes us think that we are a special team and we can do something special."

Italy led 50-48 in the fourth quarter and the crowd of 9,232 that was made up of predominantly fans of the European nation was whipped into a frenzy. Then the U.S. went on a 7-0 run to take a 55-50 advantage.

The Italians got within three and star forward Cecilia Zandalasini had a chance to tie it at the buzzer, but her 3-pointer was off. She apologized after the game for being emotional toward an official for not calling a foul on the final possession.

"I would like to apologize for how I reacted in the end," Zandalasini said. "It was a lot of emotions today, but I should have kept them inside of me a little better."

The Italians don't have much time to analyze what went wrong in the final few minutes against the U.S. with a key game against China on Monday.

"We have another very important game tomorrow. So now we've shown what we're capable of," Zandalasini said. "But we want to keep going and not just stop here and just lose our head on this game. It's still a very, very long tournament."

Zandalasini scored 14 points to lead Italy, which was one of the rare teams to actually have a .500 or better record against the U.S., going 1-1 before Sunday.

"I think we showed that tonight we deserved a spot in this tournament on this big stage," Zandalasini said. "I'm so proud of my team. and I think, we have a great coach that believes in us and we really play our hearts out."

articles.title: 3 Florida State Players that Need to Be Impactful vs. SMU
articles.summary: Florida State needs three of their most important players, QB Ashton Daniels, WR Duce Robinson and DL Mandrell Desir, to be more impactful on the field again...
articles.body:
Florida State Seminoles and the SMU Mustangs will face off for only the secondtime ever on Monday, and for the first time within thefriendly confines of Doak Campbell Stadium.

TheSeminoles have the advantage of having played a game already, a week zerovictory over New Mexico State. The Labor Day battle will be the first game ofthe season for SMU, in addition to being a road game and the conference openerfor both teams. The pressure tr is on the Mustangs.

SMU is rankedNo. 19 in the country, and considered by many to be the second-best team in theACC this season, behind the Miami Hurricanes. In their first meeting, in 2024, SMUscored 28 points in the second-half to beat the Seminoles 42-16.

To avoid arepeat of that subpar performance, three Seminole players will be need to stepup and be impactful if Florida State is to secure a victory over the talented Mustangssquad on Monday.

Danielscompleted 63 percent of his passes against New Mexico State, and threw for 202yards and accounted for two touchdowns. A solid performance. But for Daniels tobe the impactful player he must be against SMU, Daniels needs to repeat his bestperformance from last season when he was at Auburn, against the No. 15 VanderbiltCommodores.

On the roadagainst the Commodores, Daniels accounted for 442 total yards and fourtouchdowns in a seven-point losing effort. That kind of dominance could propelthe Seminoles to victory over the Mustangs.

As one ofthe best receivers in college football, and the ACC, Robinson is a talented 6-foot-6weapon that coach Mike Norvell must unleash on the SMU defense. Robinson was a1,000-yard receiver and averaged 19.30 yards per catch last season, and was a first-teamAll-ACC performer. Against New Mexico State, Robinson caught three passes for50 yards, but did not score any touchdowns. In the offensive game plan againstSMU, Robinson needs more targets.

He is amismatch made in heaven against opposing defenders, and pulled down 18contested catches a season ago. That is the most of any returning receiver inthe ACC, and that is how Norvell should exploit the SMU defense.

Robinsonmust conjure up a repeat performance of his best game against a conference opponent from lastseason, Wake Forest. Against the Demon Deacons, Robinson caught fivecatches for 148 yards and a touchdown, and averaged 29.60 yards per catch,shredding the Wake Forest pass defense.

Will the2025 version of Mandrell Desir please stand up? Last season as a true freshman,Desir led the team in tackles (57), sacks (6.5) and tackles for loss (7.5). Desirwas uncharacteristically quiet against New Mexico, borderline non-existent, andposted just four tackles with zero sacks and zero tackles for loss. Norvell andthe Seminoles need the defensive monster inside Desir to manifest itself andterrorize the Mustangs into submission.

As statedabove, all three of these players have the talent to produce and dominate oncollege football's biggest stage. It is imperative that they step up and make theirpresence felt early and often if Florida State is to come away with a victoryover the No. 19 Mustangs.

articles.title: Guitarist and wrestler Andy Williams dead at 48
articles.summary: Andy Williams has died after collapsing during a wrestling match.
articles.body:
Andy 'The Butcher' Williams has died after collapsing during a wrestling match. He was 48. All Elite Wrestling announced his death on social media on Sunday.

"A trailblazing musician with Every Time I Die and Atomic Rule, Williams made a successful transition into the world of professional wrestling and was incredibly respected by his peers both in and out of the ring," the promoter wrote in a tribute post.

"Our condolences go out to Williams' family, friends and fans."

Williams' agent confirmed his death to Pennsylvania broadcaster KDKA-TV, saying, "He was a wonderful man, and I will miss him every day."

Hours before the tragic news broke, Enjoy Wrestling shared that Williams had "collapsed at the end of his match" with tag team partner Jesse Guilmette, AKA The Blade, at a venue in Millvale, Pennsylvania.

"Our doctors on staff tended to him immediately, administering CPR until the ambulance arrived," the event organiser shared on social media. "We sent everyone home and are at the hospital now waiting for more information. Thanks to everyone who helped and has reached out."

According to dispatch audio obtained by TMZ, Williams allegedly "hit his head on a ring post" during the match.

The Office of the Allegheny County Medical Examiner confirmed to People magazine that Williams died in the hospital at 9:43 pm local time, about an hour after the incident occurred.

Before joining the wrestling world in 2019, Williams played guitar with the band Every Time I Die. He formed a new band, Atomic Rule, in 2023.

"Anyone who's written a song can wrestle a wrestling match," he said on the HardLore podcast in April.

"Putting a song together is just like putting a wrestling match together. There's ups and downs."

articles.title: Frances Tiafoe Rises to the Occasion Again in New York to Reach US Open Quarterfinals
articles.summary: Frances Tiafoe is a quarterfinalist at the US Open once again after overcoming 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev 7-6 6-4 7-6 in one of the best performances of t...
articles.body:
Frances Tiafoe is a quarterfinalist at the US Open once again after overcoming 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev 7-6 6-4 7-6 in one of the best performances of the tournament so far.

With the win, Tiafoe confirmed his place in the last eight in New York for the fourth time in the last five years. The American continues to play his best tennis at the biggest tournament in his country, now 10-0 in his career at Louis Armstrong Stadium.

Frances Tiafoe Overcomes Medvedev in Statement Victory

Entering the match down 6-1 in the head-to-head against Medvedev, Tiafoe got off to the worst possible start. Showing his nerves, he got broken in the very first game. But Tiafoe quickly regrouped to get back on serve immediately.

The first set saw each player break the other's serve three times, with Medvedev notably failing to serve out the set. Ultimately, the set went to a tiebreak, where Tiafoe raised his level considerably to comprehensively win the tiebreak and go up a set.

From there, with the home crowd and momentum of the first set behind him, Tiafoe kept dictating play from the baseline in this contest. While Medvedev did well to stay with him at the start of the second set, the American's level ultimately proved too much for the former World No. 1 as he got his serve broken. Unlike the first set, just one break of serve was enough in the second.

The third set was arguably the one in which both players played their best tennis. The players exchanged early breaks of serve, but from there, they each played a clean set of tennis. Once again, though, Tiafoe was the more dominant player on both his serve and return. A tiebreak was needed to settle the third set, and after some back-and-forth points, Medvedev found himself with a set point.

But Tiafoe did not want to extend the match any longer. The American first saved the set point with a brilliant point that tested both his baseline consistency and volleying ability. He then got himself a crucial mini-break, going up a match point on his serve. And Tiafoe just needed one match point in this match. He ultimately closed out what many had thought would be his toughest test yet this tournament in a dominant straight-sets victory.

Many wondered entering the match how Frances Tiafoe would tackle a matchup that has historically been his worst. But the American showed no signs of worry, remaining steadfast from the baseline when needed. He also incorporated his superior net skills and targeted Medvedev's second serve exceptionally well, with the Russian winning just 37% of his points behind his second serve.

This result now sets up an all-American quarterfinal, as Frances Tiafoe is set to take on Alex Michelsen. That means at least one American will be present in this year's US Open semifinals. The pair have faced off against each other twice before, with Tiafoe winning both meetings in straight sets.

As for Medvedev, he goes back to the drawing board after what felt like a sign that he was turning a page following his earlier performances in the tournament . The Russian had not dropped a set entering this match and looked back to playing at his best level again. But after this result, his level remains in flux as he ends what has undoubtedly been one of his worst-ever North American hard-court summers with more questions than answers.
